## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up at `8cf1ce64`, reassessing the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13006#issuecomment-5790835479) after the [author's update](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13006#issuecomment-5805745163).

**Verified:** both scope limits from the earlier review are addressed for the updater itself. Two narrower gaps remain around the reachability probe and a failed suspend, and the new concurrency test does not detect removal of the lock.

| Earlier point | Status at `8cf1ce64` |
|---|---|
| Suspension was best-effort (older shell or failed IPC) | **Resolved** for the suspend call. A reachable shell that rejects or times out on `setLocalPluginWatch false`, including an older shell that answers "Function not found.", now stops the update before the checkout moves. The `ping` probe before it still fails open (below). |
| Overlapping updaters not protected as a group | **Resolved** for `omarchy plugin update` processes sharing the per-user lock. `omarchy-plugin-remove` and `omarchy-plugin-add` still request rescans without the lock, which the PR description already names as follow-up work. |
| Earlier verified watcher behavior | **Still holds.** The QML watcher logic is unchanged apart from comments. Suspension now starts after fetch, diff and confirmation. Fetch writes only under `.git/`, which the registry ignores. |

**Verified in isolated stub runs:** the new regression test passes at this head (5 of 5 runs) and fails on the base and on the previously reviewed head. With stubbed shell IPC and two updaters on different plugins, this head keeps the second updater blocked while the first is mid-update. The previously reviewed head lets the second updater resume the watcher while the first is still writing.

### Reachability probe treats a starting or unresponsive shell as absent

`omarchy-shell shell ping >/dev/null 2>&1` sets `SHELL_AVAILABLE=0` on any failure. The wrapper distinguishes "not running", "not ready" and "not responding" on stderr, but the updater discards stderr and treats all three as "no shell". Through the real `bin/omarchy-shell` over a stubbed `qs`:

```text
qs reply to ping                       updater result
"Not ready to accept queries yet."  →  exit 0, checkout moved, only ping sent
no reply within the 2 s timeout     →  exit 0, checkout moved, only ping sent
"Function not found." on suspend    →  exit 1, checkout unchanged
```

**Impact:** a shell that has just started, including Quickshell relaunching itself after a crash, or one whose main thread is blocked for more than 2 s, gets no suspension and no explicit rescan. That case falls back to the pre-PR behavior for this update. The window is narrow, and it is not a new failure mode.

**Suggested change:** treat only the wrapper's "not running" result as "no shell", and fail closed (or retry briefly) on "not ready" or "not responding". Distinct wrapper exit codes, or checking the ping's stderr, would allow that.

### Failed suspend request sends no compensating resume

`WATCH_SUSPENDED=1` and `trap cleanup EXIT` are set only after `setLocalPluginWatch false` returns success. When that call times out, the updater exits with "not responding" and no resume request is sent (reproduced with a stubbed `qs`). By Quickshell's IPC server code, a stalled shell could still apply the queued suspension after the updater exits. That late application was not reproduced on a live shell.

**Impact:** if it happens, local plugin hot reload stays off until the shell restarts or a later update resumes it. No crash path was identified.

**Suggested change:** mark the suspension as attempted and arm the EXIT trap before sending the request, so every exit after an attempt sends a best-effort resume. `setLocalPluginWatch(true)` is idempotent in the QML.

**Optional test improvement:** the overlapping-update case in `test/shell.d/plugin-update-watch-test.sh` still passes 5 of 5 with `exec 9>` and `flock 9` removed. The first updater has already merged before it blocks in validation, so an unlocked second updater sees "up to date", never suspends, and produces the asserted counts. Pointing the second updater at a different plugin, or asserting that `flock -n "$OMARCHY_PLUGIN_UPDATE_LOCK" true` fails while the first is blocked, makes the case fail without the lock.

---

**Test scope:** source comparison of the base, previously reviewed head and current head, plus the relevant Quickshell IPC and `Process` source (read at v0.2.1 and v0.3.1) and util-linux `flock`. Sandboxed runs used real git, `flock` and the updater, with stubbed shell IPC (the real `omarchy-shell` wrapper over a stubbed `qs` where stated) and a stubbed validator. No live Quickshell or desktop session was run, so the QML watcher path and the reported crash fix remain unverified at runtime.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
